<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Farm Partnerships of the Harvest Expansion Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our stance might be.

It's still unclear how this will boost crop supply, reduce demand, and expand farmer choices. It doesn’t make sense to us for the state to take over a deteriorating irrigation network instead of investing in rural education.

We lack sufficient details. Several points are intriguing and deserve further analysis. Governor Vikram needs to release the specifics soon so everyone can grasp the full impact. For example, what happens to the existing procurement contracts? Can they be transferred to Harvest Expansion? Will all farmers in Pune retain their right to choose suppliers going forward?

The recent developments underscore the urgent need to ensure farmers can independently decide their sourcing options. We know the government is struggling to find the right approach. The solution is to offer farmers more options, not fewer.

We cannot support it until we are certain our dues will be paid in full. If payments fall short, it’s highly likely that we will face forced insolvency.

It’s unfortunate this deal wasn’t finalized sooner. It could have saved significant costs and difficulties.

Why is the irrigation network purchase included in this agreement? It might not even materialize. Keep it simple — manage the shortfall through securitization and the refund from AgriIndia’s trading desk, and move forward.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Southern Maharashtra
Harvest Expansion Memorandum of Understanding:

? Commitment to Supply Crops — AgriIndia will maintain its existing processing facilities and other production assets and commit them to supply crops under regulated cost-plus terms for 10 years.

? GreenFields — Shivansh Dugar will dedicate the entire output of GreenFields Farm (one of Shivansh Dugar’s private farms) to the Harvest Expansion on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of GreenFields is to be operational by 14 August 2024. If not operational by then, Shivansh Dugar will incur a ₹15 crore penalty.
